properties.statement: Each failed identity/covering-family approach transports solvability exclusively through fixed-modulus congruence relations, which quadratic reciprocity confines to eliminating non-residues, so every one of them stalls on exactly the quadratic-residue survivor classes.

supporting_passages.quote: no finite covering eliminates quadratic-residue classes
exceptional set is thin but infinite and protected by the QR wall
every failed family here preserves the quadratic-residue wall.

properties.preserved_distinctions: It does not merge the local single-identity mechanism (es-01, one class at a time, constructive), the global existential covering search (es-02), and the density-aggregation posture (es-10, counts survivors rather than covering them); es-08 remains a meta-level obstruction analysis, not a construction. They share only the congruence-carried transport of solvability.
properties.contrast_check: The partial-success es-12 also builds a congruence system, but it explicitly designs its admitted congruences to avoid quadratic residues ('admitted congruences avoid quadratic residues') and its coverage remains self-declared conjectural — consistent with the property marking a real wall rather than a shared topic. Other partial successes (es-04, es-09, es-11) do not rely on congruence transport as their solvability carrier.
properties.falsification: Exhibiting a fixed-modulus congruence identity family in the notes (or a new one) that provably covers a quadratic-residue class, or a failed approach in this family whose stall point is unrelated to the quadratic-residue classes, would refute the property.

properties.statement: Several failed approaches measure progress by a quantity (finite verification bound, average solution count, exceptional-set density) whose mode of improvement structurally cannot reach the universal 'every n' statement, so improving the number never closes the conjecture.

supporting_passages.quote: polylog average growth is too slow to force existence
finite verification is not a proof for all n
Sharpens almost-all; does not reach all.

properties.preserved_distinctions: It does not merge the mechanisms: es-05 is global, probabilistic ensemble averaging over primes; es-07 is local, deterministic per-instance certification by bounded search; es-10 is local-to-global class assembly with a density payoff. Only the shape of the boundary (quantitative measure cannot reach universality) is shared, not the operators.
properties.contrast_check: The partial-success es-06 partially shares this property ('Almost-all, not all.'), which weakens it as pure failure structure; however es-06 is the only contrast case, and the other partial successes (es-04, es-09, es-11, es-12) do not have quantitative-measure boundaries, so the property retains some discrimination.
properties.falsification: Showing that one of these measures can in principle force universality (e.g., upgrading the averaging bound to at least polynomial growth so a positive average forces existence, or a density argument that provably reaches zero) would refute the property.

properties.statement: The failed and partially failed constructive approaches reason class-locally or instance-locally and provide no global organization that couples residue classes or solved instances into a structure bearing on the unsolved ones.

supporting_passages.quote: Per-class explicit denominators; classes never coupled.
Per-n divisor search; no global organization of the solution set.
The mechanism is local and deterministic per `n`

properties.preserved_distinctions: It does not merge the operations: es-01 applies a closed-form polynomial identity per residue class with no search; es-03 enumerates divisors of an n-dependent quantity through a nonlinear factorization identity; es-07 performs exhaustive bounded search with sieving. Their locality is shared; their operators, auxiliary objects, and search character are not.
properties.contrast_check: The partial successes lean the other way: es-04 is mixed-locality, es-06 and es-09 are global, es-11 is mixed and explicitly links classes ('structural constraints link residue classes'). This asymmetry supports locality-without-coupling as failure-associated structure, though es-04's mixed locality shows locality alone is not the whole story.
properties.falsification: Demonstrating that one of these three mechanisms in fact induces cross-class or cross-instance coupling that constrains the survivor classes (e.g., a factorization-scheme lattice organization with global consequences) would refute the property.

properties.statement: The class-aggregation approaches inherit solvability only from the per-class polynomial identities they assemble and create no solvability in any class that lacks its own identity, so aggregation enlarges coverage but cannot touch the survivor classes.

supporting_passages.quote: Local identities aggregated into a global thinness statement.

properties.preserved_distinctions: It does not merge their goals or modes: es-02 seeks an exact finite covering of all of Z (existential, all-or-nothing), while es-10 accepts a non-empty leftover and bounds its density. They share only that assembly preserves, rather than generates, per-class solvability.
properties.contrast_check: The partial-success es-12 shares the inheritance pattern (it preserves 'polynomial-identity solvability per form'), and its completeness is correspondingly self-declared conjectural — it has not demonstrably escaped the property, so the contrast neither refutes nor cleanly strengthens it; this is the main reason the property is ranked last.
properties.falsification: Exhibiting an aggregation or covering construction that yields a certified solution for an n in a class covered by no member identity (solvability created by the assembly itself) would refute the property.
